PRIMARY BLOCKER — no agent loop in the pinned repository. package.json at the pinned commit: name '@openhands/agent-canvas', version 1.24.0, description 'Agent Canvas UI for OpenHands - run AI coding agents with a visual interface'. The tree is a React Router + Electron frontend (src/, vite.config.ts, electron/); there is no Python package (no pyproject.toml/setup.py) and no agent/runtime code — the only Python files are .github CI scripts, tests/e2e mock servers, and tools/canvas_ui_tool.py.

Docs confirm the split. docs/architecture.md L3: 'Agent Canvas is a React and TypeScript frontend for running and monitoring OpenHands agents across local, remote, and hosted environments.' L23: 'The primary backend is the OpenHands Agent Server (github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/tree/main/openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server)' — i.e. the agent loop lives in a DIFFERENT repository (OpenHands/software-agent-sdk), which is not the pinned/enumerated framework repo.

bin/agent-canvas.mjs L6-7/L62: 'Agent-server via uvx' / 'Runs the full stack with agent-server and automation backend via uvx' — the executable agent is an external package fetched at install time at a launcher-default version, not code at the pinned commit; a run would not be a run of the pinned artifact.

SHIM-IMPOSABILITY: within the pinned artifact there is no tool-execution layer at all, hence no supported plug point to substitute the harness web_fetch/file_write/shell_exec callables as the agent's tools. OpenHands agents (via the external Agent Server) execute their own bash/file/browser tools inside their own runtime/workspace; the deterministic shim semantics (fixed bytes, unknown-url error, header pass-through) cannot be imposed without modifying an external codebase — benchmark-side alteration, barred by TASKS.md/rubric sec.5.

SUPPORTING BLOCKER — runtime environment: README launch options are (1) host agent-server via uvx, (2) Docker sandbox, (3) multiple Docker sandboxes. On this VM: 'docker: command not found' (no Docker binary, docker info fails), and 'uv: command not found' (no uvx for option 1). node v24.20.0 / npm 10.9.4 are present but only serve the UI.
